subject: Post-demo recap: recommended models, safety checks, and next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@zenwell.health>, Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@zenwell.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: recommended models, safety checks, and next steps

Hi Asha / Jordan — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we keep momentum heading into your security review: 

Call highlights:
- Use case: clinical triage + patient-facing FAQ that must avoid giving prescriptive medical advice.
- Key constraints: sub-second 95th percentile latency for short queries, PII never leaves your VPC for the private deployment, and strict audit logs for all inference.
- Success metrics: <2% unsafe-generation rate on our safety eval, <10% false-positive refusals on benign FAQs, and cost target ~ $0.0005 per short token.

Recommended short-list for initial PoC (based on today’s sample prompts):
1) Llama-3-Chat-34B (int8) — best balance for nuance and refusal behavior (baseline).
2) RedOpt-13B (quantized) — lower cost; acceptable on FAQ-style answers but requires prompt tuning for sensitive refusals.
3) RedSafe-7B-finetuned — highest precision on refusal heuristics (recommended for rapid safety-start).

Attached I’m sending: a) a short evaluation benchmark (CSV) comparing throughput/latency/cost, b) sample prompt sets we used in the demo, and c) a one-pager PoC requirements doc you can share with procurement.

Safety / refusal notes (quick):
- We ran a targeted refusal eval that includes 450 synthetic clinical prompts and 120 seeded edge-cases. RedSafe-7B had the fewest unsafe outputs but required stronger temperature/clamp limits to avoid hallucinations.
- For ZenWell’s use case we recommend: conservative system prompts + explicit refusal templates + a two-tier fallback (model refusal -> static canned guidance -> handoff to care team).

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll provision a private PoC environment (VPC) and load the RedSafe-7B image for you to test — needs an SOW sign-off and a short procurement form.
2) Your team shares the security questionnaire (or we can start the self-serve connector to your KMS).
3) Technical POC call: can we tentatively book Wed 9/17 10am PT for model walk-through and prompt tuning?

If that timing works, I’ll send a calendar invite and drop the Drive links for the eval set. Thanks again — I’ll be standing by for the questionnaire and procurement contact.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@zenwell.health>, Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@zenwell.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: recommended models, safety checks, and next steps

Asha — great questions. Short answers here and more detail in the attached one-pager & benchmark CSV.

1) Audit logs: we can enable customer-managed log shipping. For Private deployments the inference logs (metadata + token-level events) remain in your VPC and can be exported to your SIEM/KMS. We do not persist raw prompts in Redwood’s control plane unless explicitly enabled for analytics.

2) Canary mode: yes — we support traffic mirroring and a canary pass that sends anonymized inputs to the PoC env and surfaces a diff report. That’s a standard step for safety tuning.

3) Quick model notes from our evals (attached CSV):
- Llama-3-Chat-34B (int8): highest quality on open-ended triage, 2.1% unsafe rate on our synthetic clinical suite, 95th pctl latency 340ms at 8 token bursts.
- RedOpt-13B: cost-efficient (40% cheaper) but shows more permissive phrasing on edge-case prompts; needs explicit safety templates.
- RedSafe-7B-finetuned: 0.6% unsafe in our seed set; best refusal precision, recommended starting point for ZenWell.

Prompt-set starter (attached): includes refusal templates we recommend embedding into the system prompt and guardrail post-processing checks (regex + classifier hooks). Sample guardrail snippet: 

System: "You are an assistant that gives general health information only and must refuse to provide prescriptive medical advice. If a user asks for diagnosis, medication, dosage, or emergency instructions, reply with a refusal and provide safe next steps (contact provider / call emergency services)."

Guardrail post-processing (example): if response contains "I suggest" or "you should", flag for manual review.

Next steps I will take today:
- Spin up the RedSafe-7B image in a private sandbox and share SSH/View-only Drive access (ETA: EOD Tue).
- Add ZenWell’s security questionnaire to our tracker and loop Product Security (Marissa).

Can Jordan confirm PO contact and whether ZenWell prefers a short SOW or a standard Master Services Agreement?

Cheers,
Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Asha Patel <asha@zenwell.health>, Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@zenwell.health>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: recommended models, safety checks, and next steps

Looping in product security notes and next operational asks. Hi Asha / Jordan — Marissa here (Product Security). A couple of quick items we’ll need from ZenWell before we stand up the private PoC: 

- Completed security questionnaire (you mentioned EOD 9/15 — if you can upload it to the Drive link Diego provided that’s ideal).
- KMS access pattern: please confirm whether you want HSM-backed keys or customer-managed KMS with key rotation windows.
- Data retention policy: confirm how long you want inference traces retained in the PoC (we recommend 30 days for tuning, then configurable to your policy).

Operationally we’ll: 
- Start a traffic mirroring canary that only runs on anonymized inputs.
- Provide a safety regression dashboard (sample link in attachments) that tracks unsafe vs refusal rates across prompt buckets.

Jordan — if we can get procurement contact + PO cadence I’ll sponsor the SOW and expedite the onboarding for the PoC.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
